Noah (noah@schittenhelm.dev), Version 2

## Abstract

Two-loop dihedral modular graph functions $C(a,b,c)$ arise in the low-energy expansion of the one-loop closed-string amplitude. We ask how many independent rational linear relations hold among $C(a,b,c)$, $E(w)$ and $\zeta(w)$ at odd weight $w$. A counting of linearly independent modular graph forms exists and predicts higher weights [C-litn4]. We find numerically that the relation space has dimension exactly 1 at weights 3 [C-modular-R1], 5 [C-modular-R1b], 7 [C-modular-R1c], 9 [C-modular-R1d] and 11 [C-modular-R7b]. The weight-9 relation is $960E(9)+\zeta(9)-2160C(4,4,1)-4320C(4,3,2)-960C(3,3,3)=0$ [C-modular-R6a]. We also verify inhomogeneous Laplace equations for $C(3,1,1)$ [C-modular-R4a], $C(2,1,1)$ [C-modular-R4b] and $C(2,2,1)$ [C-modular-R4c]. Holomorphic identities and an eta-quotient span table for $N \le 30$ are certified exactly [C-modular-R8]. The method is 32-digit evaluation at verifier-chosen points [C-modell], an exact leading Laurent coefficient, and a singular-value gap for completeness [C-modular-R1]. All modular-graph-function statements are numerical observations, not proofs, and are checked at 4 points only [C-modell].

## Introduction

Modular graph functions are lattice sums over $p=m\tau+n$. They arise as coefficients of the low-energy expansion of the one-loop closed-string amplitude. Identities among them were proved for weights below six [C-litn1], and all weight-six identities and all dihedral weight-seven identities were obtained and proven [C-litn3]. They satisfy Laplace eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series [C-litn5]. A counting of linearly independent modular graph forms confirms partial results and gives predictions for higher, hitherto unexplored weights [C-litn4]. Basis decompositions of two- and three-point modular graph forms are available [C-litn9].

The open question is the exact relation space among $C(a,b,c)$, $E(w)$ and $\zeta(w)$ at weights 9 [C-modular-R6e] and 11 [C-modular-R7b], together with explicit relations.

**Contribution.** We determine the relation space numerically at the odd weights 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11, with an explicit relation at each [C-modular-R1] [C-modular-R1b] [C-modular-R1c] [C-modular-R1d] [C-modular-R7b]. We verify Laplace equations for three functions [C-modular-R4a] [C-modular-R4b] [C-modular-R4c]. We certify holomorphic string-theory identities exactly by Sturm bounds [C-modular-R5a].

**Summary of results.**

- The weight-3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 observations show a relation space of dimension exactly 1 at each weight [C-modular-R1] [C-modular-R1b] [C-modular-R1c] [C-modular-R1d] [C-modular-R7b].

- The weight-11 relation was not found in a targeted literature search [C-modular-R7a].
- The Laplace observations give eigenvalue equations with Eisenstein and zeta sources [C-modular-R4a] [C-modular-R4b] [C-modular-R4c] [C-modular-R4d].
- The propositions on holomorphic identities (Jacobi, $\theta_{E8}$, $\theta_{D16}$, $\Delta$, $j$) are exact Sturm-bound certificates [C-modular-R5a] [C-modular-R5b] [C-modular-R5c] [C-modular-R5d] [C-modular-R5g] [C-modular-R5h].
- The eta-quotient span table for $N \le 30$ is exact and exhaustive [C-modular-R8].

## Model and assumptions

All parameters are fixed in [C-modell].

- Holomorphic expansion variable: $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$. Eisenstein series are normalised by $a_0=1$, $E_k=1-\frac{2k}{B_k}\sum\sigma_{k-1}(n)q^n$ [C-modell].

 The eta-span table is exact and exhaustive [C-modular-R8].

All modular-graph-function statements are numerical observations at 4 verifier points [C-modell]. None is a theorem. No weight-11 relation was found in the targeted search [C-modular-R7b].

(i) Prove the weight-9 and weight-11 relations [C-modular-R6e] [C-modular-R7b].
(ii) Decide the weight-6 relation space with a basis and precision that meet the gap criterion [C-neg1].
(iii) Find a feasible route to the full ten-function weight-11 basis [C-neg3].
(iv) Determine the relation space at weights beyond those studied here [C-litn4].

- *Completeness.* The dimension of the relation space is read off from a singular-value gap of the normalised value matrix. Singular values below 1e-24 count as kernel, and those above 1e-8 count as non-kernel [C-modular-R1].
- *Laplace equations.* These are checked by finite differences at tolerance 1e-14 [C-modell] [C-modular-R4a].

**Trusted base.** The Sturm-bound coefficient comparison is exact. By contrast, the evaluation of the modular graph functions, the finite-difference Laplacian and the singular-value decomposition are floating-point computations [C-modell]. Relations among modular graph functions are therefore numerical observations at the verifier points, not theorems.

**Basis origin.** The weight-11 hypothesis basis originated in a human-guided exploration and was then verified by the code verifier [C-modular-R7a].

**Execution.** The work was carried out in an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which every statement is accepted only after code verification. Details are given in Appendix A.

## Holomorphic identities from string partition functions

*Notation.* We write $\eta(d)=\eta(d\tau)$ and $\theta(d)=\sum_n q^{dn^2}$. $\Delta(d)$ denotes the discriminant form scaled to $\Delta(d\tau)$, and $j=E_4^3/\Delta$ [C-modular-R5h]. $\theta_{E8}$ and $\theta_{D16}$ denote the theta series of the two heterotic lattices [C-modular-R5d]. Each identity below is an exact Sturm-bound certificate: all terms lie in the stated space of modular forms, and the listed $q$-coefficients vanish exactly.

::: proposition [Jacobi identity, weight 2]
On $\Gamma_0(4)$: $\theta(1)^4=\eta(2)^{20}\eta(1)^{-8}\eta(4)^{-8}$ [C-modular-R5a].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{11}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 1 (index 6) [C-modular-R5a].
*Novelty status:* already stated in the literature [C-litn7] [C-modular-R5a].

::: proposition [Jacobi identity, weight 1]
On $\Gamma_0(4)$: $\theta(1)^2=\eta(2)^{10}\eta(1)^{-4}\eta(4)^{-4}$ [C-modular-R5b].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{10}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 1/2 (index 6) [C-modular-R5b].
*Novelty status:* already stated in the literature [C-litn7] [C-modular-R5b].

::: proposition [$E_8$ lattice]
On $\Gamma_0(1)$: $\theta_{E8}=E_4$ [C-modular-R5c].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{10}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 1/3 (index 1) [C-modular-R5c]. This reproduces a classical result and was preregistered as a validation anchor (no claim of novelty) [C-modular-R5c].

::: proposition [Heterotic lattices]
On $\Gamma_0(1)$: $\theta_{E8}^2=\theta_{D16}$ [C-modular-R5d], $\theta_{E8}^2=E_4^2$ [C-modular-R5e], and $\theta_{E8}^2=E_8$ [C-modular-R5f].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{10}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 2/3 (index 1) [C-modular-R5d] [C-modular-R5e] [C-modular-R5f]. This reproduces a classical result and was preregistered as a validation anchor (no claim of novelty) [C-modular-R5d].

::: proposition [Discriminant]
On $\Gamma_0(1)$: $1728\,\Delta(1)-E_4^3+E_6^2=0$ [C-modular-R5g].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{11}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 1 (index 1) [C-modular-R5g].
*Novelty status:* already stated in the literature [C-litn8] [C-modular-R5g].

::: proposition [$j$-function]
On $\Gamma_0(1)$: $j\,\Delta(1)=E_4^3$ [C-modular-R5h].
:::

*Certificate.* The coefficients $q^0$ to $q^{11}$ vanish and the Sturm bound is 1 (index 1) [C-modular-R5h]. This reproduces a classical result and was preregistered as a validation anchor (no claim of novelty) [C-modular-R5h].

For all $N \le 30$, holomorphic eta quotients with trivial character span $M_4(\Gamma_0(N))$ exactly for $N \in \{2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30\}$ and not for $N \in \{1, 3, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 21, 23, 29\}$ [C-modular-R8].

The suspected cause is that the working precision is too low relative to the coefficient height [C-neg3].

## Discussion, limitations and open questions

All statements about modular graph functions are numerical observations at 4 verifier points [C-modell], and none is a theorem. Residuals far below the tolerance 1e-24, the exact leading Laurent coefficient and the singular-value gaps make accidental relations unlikely, but they do not prove an identity [C-modular-R6a] [C-modular-R1d]. The weight-6 case remains undecided [C-neg1]. The literature status of the weight-9 relation is inconclusive, and the relation may be implied by the counting of [C-litn4] [C-modular-R6e]. No weight-11 relation was found in the targeted search [C-modular-R7b].

Open questions:

(i) Prove the weight-9 and weight-11 relations [C-modular-R6e] [C-modular-R7b].
(ii) Decide the weight-6 relation space using a basis and a precision that meet the gap criterion [C-neg1].
(iii) Find a feasible route to the full ten-function weight-11 basis [C-neg3].
(iv) Determine the relation space at weights beyond those studied here [C-litn4].
